title: Ship the explicit 23-variable nonspectrahedral cone plus its exact 100x100 SDP lift as a paired solver test instance
summary: This is the only known cone that is provably not spectrahedral yet has a certified exact SDP lift, so native hyperbolic solves and lifted SDP solves must agree exactly. I built it and verified it numerically. The lift boundary matches the true boundary to relative error at most 1e-5 on 34 rays, including singular-X boundary points. On 19 random instances the native barrier, Clarabel and SCS agree to about 4e-7. The lifted optimum is degenerate (rank 25 of 100), and Clarabel reports optimal_inaccurate on 18 of 19.
beneficiaries: Developers of hyperbolic-programming and moment-lift solvers (DDS, Hypatia, alfonso, research first-order codes); a small community
first_step: Port /home/claude/work/repos/scratch_optimization/hyp_cone.py (q, slice pencil, lift builder) into LMCO .mat format, and encode q as a division-free (Berkowitz) straight-line program for DDS.
measurement: Native vs lifted objective agreement, iteration counts and status flags. Baseline: native barrier median 71 Newton steps and 0.2 s; Clarabel median 9 iterations and 2.5 s, 18/19 inaccurate; SCS median 225 iterations and 0.74 s; max objective difference about 4e-7.
risks: Tiny audience. Says nothing about scale. The lift paper is not Lean-formalized (numerics support it). The lift's 307 auxiliary variables include 126 that never appear in the matrix.

title: Treat 'hyperbolic programs are strictly more expressive than SDP' as a solver-roadmap driver
summary: The only proven non-liftable hyperbolicity cone has m=330, r=20N-1 with N>12,960, so ambient dimension and degree are each about 6.7e10. Every hyperbolicity cone used in practice or benchmarks is known liftable or merely large-lift (derivative relaxations: Saunderson-Parrilo; elementary-symmetric cones: Branden). DDS 3.0 already argues for native solvers on lift size, not lift existence, so no solver team (MOSEK, Clarabel, SCS, Hypatia) faces this decision.
beneficiaries: None in practice; theoretical justification only
first_step: None. At most, cite the result in hyperbolic-solver documentation as an existence-level justification.
risks: Overclaiming practical relevance. The non-liftable paper is not Lean-formalized.

title: Update textbooks, surveys and benchmark docs: MIRUP is false and OPT+C bin packing is NP-hard
summary: Lean-checked: for every c there is an instance with integral LP=B and OPT>B+c (sizes >1/6), and an OPT+C polynomial algorithm exists iff P=NP. This closes Williamson-Shmoys Ch.17 Problem 3 (conditionally on P!=NP) and the Scheithauer-Terno MIRUP conjecture. Witnesses are tower-sized: P0=100^11, d>=2.4e27 tree phases, denominators [100(D*+1)]^L. The hardness needs exponentially large denominators, so it says nothing about poly-capacity instances such as BPPLIB. No solver change is needed; ceil(LP) remains a valid bound, and VPSolver has no IRUP or MIRUP logic.
beneficiaries: Approximation-algorithms researchers (stop seeking OPT+O(1)); cutting-stock theorists; textbook and survey authors
first_step: Send a short note to the cutting-stock community (Scheithauer, Kartak, Rietz) and the BPPLIB maintainers, stating precisely: MIRUP is false with integral LP; witnesses are astronomically large; ceil(LP) practice is unaffected.
measurement: Errata, edition and survey updates; citations
risks: Negligible. Readers may wrongly infer a practical impact on branch-and-price or arc-flow; the note must say there is none.

title: Find the smallest bin-packing / cutting-stock instance with OPT - LP >= 2
summary: With MIRUP disproved, the size of the smallest witness is a well-posed open problem. The best computational gap remains 6/5 (non-proper) and 1.1 (proper, Kartak-Ripatti 2019). The paper's competing-tree reduction gives no usable size bound, so new ideas or large computational searches are needed. This is a real theory item but has no practical consequence, because ceil(LP) is used only as a lower bound.

targets.name: Kartak et al., minimal proper non-IRUP instances (arXiv 1405.5988)

first_step: Check whether the vertex-cover/K4 mechanism admits a version with c=1 and small d (the d>=72K requirement comes from the P0 score slack), or seed Kartak-Ripatti search heuristics with gap-amplifying compositions of known 6/5 instances.
measurement: Explicit instance with verified LP and OPT, gap >= 2
risks: May need tower-scale instances in any construction; open-ended

title: Use the MIRUP counterexample family as benchmark instances, or change branch-and-price/arc-flow stopping rules
summary: The gap instances cannot be written down. The competing-tree gadget runs 2d-1 (about 4.8e27) phases, with leaf counts 1 -> 2 -> 10 -> 699,050 -> about 2^699050 within the first four, so item denominators are tower-sized. Exact solvers use ceil(LP) only as a valid lower bound; nothing relies on OPT <= ceil(LP)+1.

title: Replace zstd COVER/FASTCOVER segment concatenation with a superstring (2-approximation) packer
summary: Verified in code: COVER_selectSegment and FASTCOVER_selectSegment maximise distinct-dmer frequency coverage, zero out covered dmers, and memcpy segments back to front. The objective is coverage under a byte budget, not superstring length. Measured on 1,278 C++ files (17.8 MB, 112,640-byte dictionary, k=200, d=8): any superstring merge of the selected segments saves at most 1.06% (COVER) or 1.29% (FASTCOVER), by a cycle-cover bound. Plain greedy already achieves 1.05% and 1.29%.
beneficiaries: None (at most about 1% of the dictionary budget could be freed, and greedy already does that)
first_step: None. If anyone wants the ~1%, a greedy overlap post-pass suffices; the paper's algorithm is unnecessary.

title: Certify k-mer superstring tools (KmerCamel) with the paper's forced-count lower bound W
summary: I implemented W (extension rules, period rule with blocking functional) and validated W <= OPT on 2,342 tiny instances, with zero violations. On k=31 k-mer sets from 100 kb of S. pneumoniae, W equals KmerCamel's existing cycle-cover bound exactly; the period rule never raises a count, and certified greedy gaps are 0-0.012%. W costs 300-440 s in Python against 0.1-0.5 s for the cycle cover. Only on subsampled synthetic tandem-repeat sets did W beat the cycle cover, by 0.3% (4,969 vs 4,955). Incidental finding not from the paper: KmerCamel greedy is 12.5% above optimum on a tandem-repeat set (OPT bracketed in [5071, 5072]); its own existing bound already certifies this.
beneficiaries: k-mer set compression researchers working on extremely repetitive sequence (satellite arrays); otherwise none
first_step: If pursued: port scs_W.py to C++ on KmerCamel's k-mer hash and evaluate on T2T centromeric satellite arrays, where the period rule could fire. Separately, report the 12.5% greedy gap on tandem-repeat sets to the KmerCamel authors (independent of this paper).
measurement: W minus cycle-cover bound, as a percentage, on repetitive real data; runtime of a C++ W
risks: Measured: no gain on genome k-mer sets and about 1000x cost. The gain appears only on short-k or pathological periodic inputs.

title: Proven optima for K_n / K_{m,n} crossing numbers: OEIS, crossing-minimization benchmarks, OGDF test oracle
summary: cr(K_n) and cr(K_{m,n}) are proven equal to the Hill and Zarankiewicz formulas for all n (Lean-checked). OEIS A000241 still lists terms only to n=14 with no 2026 'proved' edit. The Star-Struck benchmark sets 'Complete' (K5-K50, 46 graphs) and 'Complete-Bip.' (666 graphs) currently measure heuristics against the best solution found, and can now report gaps to proven optima. OGDF heuristic tests can use Z(n) as a valid lower-bound oracle for all n (today only K10 >= 60).
beneficiaries: Graph-drawing heuristic researchers, OGDF maintainers, OEIS readers
first_step: Submit the OEIS edit citing the Lean-checked theorem, and open an OGDF PR adding K_n/K_{m,n} lower-bound sanity tests from the formulas.
measurement: OEIS entry updated; benchmark papers report exact optimality gaps on the 712 complete and complete-bipartite instances
risks: Low value: heuristics already matched the Z(n) upper-bound drawings. The result does not cover rectilinear (straight-line) crossing numbers.

title: Use exact cr(K_n) for VLSI, photonic or layout design decisions
summary: Multilayer layouts make crossings free, and straight-line drawings use the rectilinear crossing number, which is larger and not settled by this result. The asymptotic constant was already known to within about 1.5%. No design decision changes.

title: Integer-programming proximity / DP state-space reduction via the Euclidean Steinitz bound
summary: The constant is C = 2 D* A0 / sigma with sigma = min{1/2, kappa*delta/(sqrt2*pi)} = 5.6e-4. That gives C >= 3554*A0, with A0 > c1*sqrt(C_phi) never quantified (about 1e4 if C_phi >= 1). An l2-ball DP beats the l_inf Steinitz bound m*Delta only when sqrt(m) > C*Delta2/Delta, i.e. m > C^2, about 1e7 constraints, far outside where (m*Delta)^m DPs run. The result is existential with no algorithm, and Aliev et al. 2026 already give an optimal Euclidean proximity bound without Steinitz.

title: Planar / bounded-treewidth flow-cut gap constants for sparsest cut or graph partitioning
summary: The planar distortion is C = 16m/(pb) with p = 2^-(2*M_pack+10) and M_pack = 2+ceil(1600R/g) = 1.6e9 (R=1e-8, g=1e-14), so C >= 2^(3.2e9), about 10^(9.6e8). The triage's figure of about 1e60 is far too small. C_k for treewidth is non-explicit (compactness). Rao's O(sqrt(log n)) is smaller for every physically possible n, and partitioners (METIS, KaHIP, Scotch) are heuristic.
beneficiaries: None in practice; approximation-algorithms theory only
